mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investing parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent corporate registrar in the foreign investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille state): notarize in the country of issue, then obtain a single Hague Apostille from the local competent authority. Path B (non-member state): notarize, then authenticate through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then complete Consular Legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that country. Paths A and B are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Incumbency of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registrar or companies registry in the jurisdiction where the foreign investor is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille state): notarize locally, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the competent authority. Path B (non-member state): notarize locally, authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE's legal representative, directors, and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor, notarized and certified by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention path: notary certification then single apostille by the issuing state's competent authority. Non-Convention path: notary certification, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization. These routes are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and constitutional documents of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, registered agent, or registrar maintaining the foreign investor's constitutional records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin state is an Apostille member: certified true copy, then Hague Apostille. If not: certified true copy, local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then Consular Legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. Only one route applies per document set.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the foreign investor's account relationships and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate banking institution of the foreign investor, with bank officer signature and official bank seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: bank notarization followed by a single apostille from the competent authority. For non-Apostille states: bank notarization, local Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmation, and Chinese Consular Legalization. Never both apostille and consular legalization on the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) beneficial owner filings, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the U.S. Non-SDN Consolidated Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List (including 1267/1988), Interpol Red Notices, World Bank Debarment List, and domestic Chinese credit enforcement and tax violations databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP), family member, or close associate, with source-of-wealth verification and upward cascade to senior compliance committee. For high-risk jurisdictions, enhanced legitimate business and source-of-funds documentation is mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Service Portal and local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) online name clearance and pre-registration module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Chinese name registration law, a registered company name must be in Chinese characters and follow a four-tier structure: (1) administrative division, (2) distinctive trade name of at least two characters, (3) industry or business characteristics, and (4) legal form suffix. For a WFOE, the registered name may not contain 'China' or 'Chinese' unless expressly approved by the State Council or competent SAMR authorities. English names may be used as trade aliases but not as the sole registered name. Phonetic transliteration must be commercially distinguishable and must not create obscene, misleading, or impermissible meanings. Arabic numerals, Latin letters, and symbols are generally prohibited in the Chinese registered name except where special administrative approval has been granted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant or its Chinese counsel must file an administrative review with the same AMR/SAMR bureau that issued the rejection within 15 days of receipt, explaining how the proposed name complies with the four-tier structure and why it is distinguishable. If the review is unsuccessful, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the next-higher market regulation authority or the local people's government within 60 days. A subsequent administrative lawsuit may be filed with the competent people's court within six months. The original name reservation is not automatically extended during the appeal, so a fresh name pre-registration should be filed in parallel only if legally permissible.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address for a logistics technology SaaS WFOE. Chinese Company Law requires a company to maintain a domicile that is its principal place of business. Local SAMR authorities normally demand a lease agreement, property ownership certificate, or landlord's permit matching the registered address. Tax authorities and banks reject mail-forwarding arrangements, and for industries involving telematics and fleet dispatch, the tax authority expects the entity to maintain books, contracts, and physical meeting capability at the registered site. Some free trade zones allow flexible address filing, but an actual physical site will still be required for tax inspection, bank account opening, and commercial substance verification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 65-70% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by municipal SAMR or tax authorities within the first 12 months of registration. Checklist: (1) company nameplate at the registered address; (2) lease agreement or property title corresponding to the exact registered address; (3) utility bills or property invoices in the company's name; (4) accessible financial records and statutory books; (5) staff presence or verifiable management personnel on site; (6) documented client/vendor contracts supporting active business operations. Failure may result in the address being marked 'unverifiable', removal from the registry, or inclusion in the national enterprise credit blacklist.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 7, 8, 14, 24, 27, 32, 38, 39, 41, 47, 49, 51, 52, 54, 62 and 90; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4, 12 and 13; Regulations on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law; Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List, 2021 edition).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the local municipal/district Administration for Market Regulation, Market Entity Registration Division, using the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Portal and National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application together with the Articles of Association; issuance of the Unified Social Credit Code Business License constitutes completion of incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for a general software/SaaS WFOE outside the Negative List. The 2023 Company Law Article 47 requires the full registered capital subscribed in the Articles to be contributed within five years from incorporation; there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement. The capital amount must be rationally matched to the business scale and industry norm, and any subsequent capital increase or decrease must be filed with SAMR and disclosed in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [CN_WFOE_LTD]. RESOLVED, that the Company adopts as its registered office the address set out in the Articles of Association filed with the local Administration for Market Regulation, and that such address shall be the legal domicile for the service of official process and governmental correspondence, to remain in force until lawfully changed by an amendment to the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscribed registered capital, being RMB [AMOUNT] divided into [NUMBER] registered capital contributions, is hereby confirmed as subscribed by the Sole Shareholder according to the Articles of Association; that the statutory obligation to make full contribution within five years from the date of incorporation, as prescribed by Article 47 of the PRC Company Law, is expressly acknowledged; and that the first and subsequent tranches of capital contributions may be called by the executive director and deposited solely into a dedicated capital contribution account of the Company at a licensed commercial bank in China. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the executive director and the general manager are jointly authorized, under such signatory mandate as the bank may require, to open current and capital accounts in the name of the Company, to execute account-opening agreements, electronic banking mandates, foreign exchange declarations, and depository instructions, to designate authorized signatories, and to terminate or vary such authorizations from time to time upon a written resolution of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [NATURAL PERSON A] is appointed executive director and legal representative, [NATURAL PERSON B] is appointed general manager, and [NATURAL PERSON C] is appointed supervisor, each with powers and duties as provided in the Articles and the PRC Company Law, the legal representative being authorized to execute registrations, applications, leases, contracts, and seal-control undertakings necessary for the operation of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the executive director and the general manager are, jointly or severally, authorized to prepare, sign, and submit all registration filings, enterprise information reports, tax registrations, social insurance declarations, bank account applications, and any statutory forms relating to the incorporation and initial licensing, and to engage legal counsel, notaries, and accountants as necessary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all acts done prior to the date of this resolution by the promoters, attorneys, and any agent of the Sole Shareholder in connection with the preparation and filing of the incorporation instruments are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved in all respects. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any two authorized officers may certify conformed copies of this resolution, and that this resolution shall be effective as a continuing delegation until revoked or superseded by a resolution of the Sole Shareholder or the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-approval of Company Name and Screening against the Foreign Investment Negative List
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal/district Administration for Market Regulation through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before submission of the establishment application, counsel shall screen the proposed business scope for the software, logistics-telematics, and data-processing activities against the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (the Negative List). The applicant shall log in to the local Administration for Market Regulation integrated enterprise registration web portal under the real-name authentication of the foreign shareholder and proposed legal representative, submit the enterprise name reservation request with at least three Chinese-language name options, and complete an online market-access declaration. For offshore entities, the certificate of incorporation and board appointment documents must be notarized at the Chinese Consulate or apostilled as applicable, and translated into Chinese; foreign individuals must submit notarized passport copies. The AMR shall verify name uniqueness, negative-list eligibility, and basic corporate contents before issuing a Name Reservation Notice.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese company name and at least three alternate name options
Notarized or apostilled certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder and passport copy
Identity document and passport photograph of the proposed legal representative
Description of the intended business scope, registered capital amount and contribution timeline
Registered office lease certificate, landlord title certificate, or letter of consent for address use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant shall revise the name components and resubmit within five business days; if the business scope is deemed to touch the Negative List, the applicant shall either adjust the scope and corporate structure or obtain approval from the competent commerce authority; any administrative refusal may be challenged through administrative reconsideration to the next-higher authority or through judicial review in a PRC court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Constitutional Instruments and Filing of the Establishment Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation via the online integrated enterprise registration system and the subsequent National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System record
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the name reservation is obtained, the Sole Shareholder shall approve the final Articles of Association, subscribe the registered capital, appoint the executive director, supervisor, and general manager, and execute the incorporation application forms. The application shall be submitted online to the local AMR integrated enterprise registration system, with the electronic Articles, foreign investment information reporting form, identity files, lease certificate, and negative-list declaration appended. The legal representative and all appointed officers shall complete online identity verification. The AMR reviews the application, confirms the Unified Social Credit Code, issues the Business License, and records the entity in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. The applicant shall check that the license description exactly mirrors the approved business scope. In municipalities that require physical filing, notarized paper copies are submitted at the same time; certified Chinese translations must accompany any foreign-language instrument.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Notice
Final Articles of Association signed by the Sole Shareholder
Foreign Investment Information Report form
Certificate of identity and apostille/notarization of foreign shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the filing agent, if used
Registered office lease and landlord ownership certificate
Appointment instruments of executive director, supervisor and general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a correction notice or suspends the application, the applicant shall cure the specified defects within ten working days by amending the Articles or correcting the identity and lease instruments and then resubmit through the same portal; if issuance of the Business License is refused, the applicant shall obtain a written refusal decision and may apply for administrative reconsideration within sixty days or institute an administrative lawsuit within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Insurance, Housing Fund and Ancillary Statutory Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Management Center; local integrated government service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Business License, the company must complete post-incorporation registrations before substantive operation. Tax registration is automatically generated under the one-license one-code reform but must be finalized with the local State Taxation Administration by selecting a tax collection mode, binding electronic invoices, and signing an online tax deposit tripartite agreement between the taxpayer, the bank and the tax authority. The employer shall register with the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau for social insurance and with the Housing Provident Fund Management Center; if foreign employees are to be hired, the company must obtain employment permits and residence or work permits. The statistics authority receives registration automatically through data sharing, and customs registration should be made if the company will later import or export fleet telematics hardware or software-bearing devices.
required_dossiers: Business License with Unified Social Credit Code
Legal representative identity and passport copy
Article of Association and board appointments
Foreign shareholder notarization or apostille and Chinese translation
Bank account opening documents or bank confirmation
Office lease and landlord consent for inspection
Social insurance and housing fund employer registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or social insurance registration reveals a mismatch in the Unified Social Credit Code or entity data, the company must coordinate data correction between AMR and the tax authority; if the electronic invoice or tripartite agreement is queried, the company shall submit the bank account confirmation and corrected articles; any late registration penalty may be mitigated by voluntary disclosure to the competent tax or labor authority within the statutory correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Bank Accounts, Capital Contribution and Direct Investment Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in China acting under the delegated authority of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Concurrently, the Company shall open a RMB basic deposit account and, if foreign currency capital is to be paid in by the overseas shareholder, a foreign exchange capital account with a licensed commercial bank in China. The bank will complete the direct investment foreign exchange registration under delegated SAFE powers, using the Business License, Unified Social Credit Code, Articles of Association, foreign investment information report, and identity documents. The shareholder must wire the subscribed capital by lawful cross-border remittance channels; the bank verifies the source of funds and credits the amount into the capital account. Funds may be used only after the bank completes authenticity and compliance review and must not be applied to transactions outside the approved business scope. Capital contributions are subject to the five-year statutory payment timeline under Article 47, and any subsequent increase of registered capital must be registered with the AMR.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Approved Articles of Association
Foreign investment information report filing receipt
Legal representative identity and board appointment documents
AML/KYC forms for the foreign shareholder ultimate beneficial owner
Proof of office address and lease agreement
Company seal and financial seal registration certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank account opening or SAFE registration is queried, the applicant shall supplement corporate ownership chain declarations, source-of-funds evidence, and updated Articles; if the bank declines, the applicant may ask for a written reason and apply to another licensed bank; if foreign exchange registration fails because of a missing or inconsistent foreign investment information report, the company must first update the report through the AMR integrated system and then reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seal Engraving, Foreign Investment Information Report Completion and Operational Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public security bureau approved seal engraving unit; AMR/MOFCOM integrated foreign investment information reporting system; local fire and workplace safety authorities for ordinary office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After capitalization, the Company shall complete the Foreign Investment Information Report formalities and prepare for operational compliance. The initial foreign investment information report is filed electronically through the integrated enterprise registration system together with the incorporation application; the company must update the report promptly upon any change of shareholder, capital, scope, or branch. The company must arrange for engraving of the company seal, financial seal, contract seal, invoice seal and legal representative seal at a licensed seal engraving enterprise approved by the local public security bureau, enter into the lease for the registered office with landlord consent, and ensure that the office address is fit for the registered physical seat. For pure software or telematics SaaS activity, no production, assembly, chemical, or warehousing license is required; the employer must nonetheless display the Business License at the office and complete standard workplace safety signage and fire equipment checks for office staff.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code
Approved Articles of Association
Foreign investment information report corrections or amendment forms, if any
Seal engraving certificate from the public security bureau approved engraver
Office lease, landlord consent and building occupancy/fire inspection documentation
Tax registration and social insurance employer registration certificates
Legal representative identity documents for seal control and authority matrix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal engraving is delayed due to invalid identity documents or expired licenses, the company must first correct the underlying AMR record; if the foreign investment information report is rejected or failed by system checks, the company shall use the correction window on the integrated reporting platform within the time limit notified by AMR/MOFCOM; where an industrial operating permit is wrongly demanded, the company may submit a legal opinion classifying the activity as ISIC 6201 pure digital/software and therefore not requiring such a permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — no industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing agency is engaged for ISIC 6201 pure software/telematics SaaS operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no sector-specific industrial operating license is required; the standard Business License, tax registration and ordinary office fire safety compliance suffice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — Ministry of Ecology and Environment oversight not triggered for pure software operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt/Not Applicable — ISIC 6201 is a computer programming and digital services activity with no manufacturing or chemical process requiring an EIA report or environmental

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic portal: STA National Electronic Tax Service Platform, accessed via the official STA website www.chinatax.gov.cn and through provincial electronic tax bureaus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Prepare foreign investor corporate documents with notarization and legalization/apostille, WFOE articles of association, registered address certificate, and board/shareholder resolutions. Step 2: Submit the WFOE establishment application through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) one-stop enterprise startup service to obtain a business license carrying the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); the USCC is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). Step 3: Complete supplementary tax registration within 30 days after business license issuance through the electronic tax platform: confirm legal entity resident status, ISIC 6201/NAICS 488490 industry classification, accounting and inventory policies, legal representative, bank accounts, shareholders, and expected annual turnover. Step 4: Determine VAT status; if expected annual VAT taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory; below the threshold the WFOE may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer or elect general VAT taxpayer status if accounting standards allow. Step 5: Apply for e-invoice issuance capability, obtain the tax control U-key/digital certificate, and configure the electronic invoice platform with the financial system. Step 6: Complete State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) registration at a designated bank for foreign-currency export proceeds. Step 7: For an actual non-resident foreign enterprise without a Chinese permanent establishment supplying taxable services into China, register for non-resident VAT withholding/tax registration through the competent provincial STA or rely on the Chinese domestic counterparty's withholding obligation; the WFOE itself, as a Chinese tax-resident legal entity, requires only the USCC/TIN rather than a separate foreign ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None with respect to pass-through or check-the-box elections; China has no entity classification election or hybrid mismatch election under general tax law. The available statutory election is VAT taxpayer status: a new WFOE below the RMB 5,000,000 general VAT registration threshold may elect small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment with simplified levy, or elect general VAT taxpayer status to recover input VAT and claim export zero-rating; once annual turnover exceeds the threshold, general VAT taxpayer status is compulsory.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Interim Regulations and the Ministry of Finance/STA Notice Cai Shui [2016] No. 36; standard general goods rate 13%, reduced rates 9% and 6%, modern services including software/SaaS applicable rate 6%, and eligible export zero-rating 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual VAT-taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; all incorporated WFOEs must complete tax registration and obtain a Unified Social Credit Code/TIN upon establishment regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA mandates the Full Digital Electronic Invoice (FDEI) regime for general VAT taxpayers; invoices must be issued through the STA electronic invoice service platform using the Unified Social Credit Code, digitally signed with the tax-control U-key, include the anti-fraud QR code, and transmit invoice data to the STA in near-real-time. High-volume issuers must integrate via the STA-authorized e-invoice API; no private paper invoice production is permitted for digitalized taxpayers, and general VAT taxpayers must use Special VAT Invoices for B2B taxable supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility for 0% VAT export treatment arises for physical goods exported from China under the PRC VAT export exemption/refund regime and for specified cross-border services consumed entirely outside mainland China. For this logistics fleet-dispatch SaaS, the WFOE must be a general VAT taxpayer, the service must be supplied to an offshore recipient, the service must be rendered and consumed outside China, the contract and payment evidence must demonstrate foreign-currency settlement, and the export zero-rating declaration must be filed through the STA e-taxation platform; physical hardware exports accompanying the SaaS require an export customs declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration of the People's Republic of China issued by the General Administration of Customs for any physical goods or hardware exported
Original Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing outbound shipment from a PRC port to the overseas destination

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent SAFE-designated bank foreign-exchange receipt and settlement voucher proving the full foreign-currency export proceeds were repatriated to the WFOE's PRC account

Digital zero-rated VAT e-invoice, export sales contract, commercial invoice, packing list, and for SaaS delivery: service agreement, server/telematics usage logs, and other evidence proving offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export zero-rating is unsubstantiated or fraudulent, the STA will claw back the zero-rated output VAT, disallow any refund/export rebate, impose daily late-payment surcharges at 0.05% per day, assess administrative penalties between 50% and 500% of the tax amount under the Law of the PRC on the Administration of Tax Collection, downgrade the taxpayer credit rating, suspend e-invoice issuance and export tax-refund eligibility, and refer serious cases for criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refunds under Article 204 of the Criminal Law; customs authorities may separately impose penalties and confiscate any wrongfully refunded amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The renminbi operates under a managed floating exchange-rate system rather than full free convertibility. Current-account transactions are broadly convertible, but each payment or receipt must be supported by genuine underlying commercial documentation and pass the bank's authenticity and matching review. The capital account remains materially controlled. A WFOE receiving foreign equity capital must first complete SAFE foreign-investment registration, then open a dedicated foreign-currency capital account at a licensed Chinese bank. Withdrawal and conversion of the capital into RMB are done through the bank under SAFE capital-account payment-convertibility mechanisms with post-registration monitoring. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are lawful after the annual audit, statutory tax settlement, and filing of the financial statements with the authorities; the bank verifies that the distribution is drawn from verified accumulated profits and that tax has been cleared. Export proceeds must be repatriated into the domestic banking system and held in a current-account foreign-currency deposit or voluntarily sold for RMB; mandatory surrender has been abolished, but the enterprise remains subject to verification of the trade receipts and reporting through the cross-border balance-of-payments system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods-export foreign-exchange income must be repatriated to a PRC bank within 90 days from the customs export declaration date, or within the due date under the contract if a later payment term has been formally applied for with SAFE. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; 100% of the export proceeds may remain in a foreign-exchange current account, and conversion into RMB is optional at the bank's prevailing interbank market rate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low - not legally viable as a primary bank. Cross-border digital EMIs such as Airwallex, Stripe, or similar non-bank payment providers are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in China and cannot open a PRC basic deposit account on behalf of the WFOE. They cannot access CNAPS or CIPS as a substitute clearing member for the entity's domestic treasury operations. Such platforms may be used only as auxiliary collection rails for overseas or e-commerce card transactions, provided the provider holds the required SAFE cross-border payment institution license. The WFOE must maintain its primary operational account, capital account, and RMB basic deposit account at a licensed Chinese commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative or a locally resident authorized person must generally appear physically in-branch to complete the face-to-face KYC interview and dual-control verification when opening the RMB basic deposit account. Pure remote consular proxy opening without an in-branch attendee is normally rejected. If the legal representative is overseas, a notarized Power of Attorney, often with consular legalization or apostille and a Chinese translation, may allow a local authorized officer to attend with the original corporate seal and resolution; the bank may still require a supplementary video interview and enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership behind the WFOE, particularly where the offshore parent holds layers of intermediate entities or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete beneficial ownership diagram tracing to named ultimate natural persons; certificates of incorporation and good standing for every intermediary entity; notarized passport copies and utility-bill proof of address for UBOs; signed UBO declaration per PRC AML rules; audited financial statements of the direct parent and ultimate parent; private bankers' reference letters from the parent's home jurisdiction; and a source-of-wealth questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SaaS fleet-dispatch business may be perceived as processing sensitive logistics telematics and personal data, triggering cybersecurity, cross-border data transfer, or national security red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements and end-user agreements; a data flow matrix showing what data is processed and where; PRC data security self-assessment or filing certificate; ICP/EDI license if a platform is operated; privacy policy and data processing addenda; evidence that telematics data is hosted in approved PRC or compliant cloud infrastructure; and a written PIPL/DSL cross-border transfer impact assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI funds may be perceived as coming from intra-group loans, third-party financing, or commingled treasury rather than genuine parent operating surplus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Parent board resolution specifically authorizing the equity capital injection; 12 months of certified parent bank statements demonstrating organic availability; a statutory declaration of capital source; the group funding policy; any intra-group loan agreement with SAFE debt registration if applicable; and confirmations that no third-party nominee or undisclosed principal funds are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-value outbound disbursements to logistics vendors, subcontractors, or software consultants could mimic trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full contract pack for each material vendor; detailed invoices and payment schedules; logistics dispatch records with geolocation data; vendor onboarding and KYC records; evidence of actual SaaS delivery and usage; PRC tax invoices and monthly VAT filings; payroll records; and a board-approved treasury cash-flow forecast mapping each disbursement to a contractual obligation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas parent remits the FDI capital via SWIFT MT103, or cross-border RMB via CIPS, into the WFOE's designated foreign-currency capital account at the domestic bank. The remittance instruction must cite the SAFE FDI registration number and use the appropriate cross-border remittance purpose code for FDI equity injection. Upon receipt, the bank performs an authenticity and compliance review, converts the proceeds into RMB at the prevailing market rate, and transfers the converted funds into the RMB capital fund account. A PRC licensed CPA thereafter issues a capital verification report evidencing the injection. All capital funds must be used strictly within the approved business scope; they may not be used for securities investment, entrusted loans, real-estate speculation, or non-business expenditures.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For software licensing, cloud hosting, logistics subcontracting, and overseas vendor payments, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 for direct credit transfers, commercial letters of credit for physical hardware or fleet-vehicle procurement, and documentary collections for moderate-risk supplier settlement. Cross-border RMB payments with Chinese counterparties or qualified foreign beneficiaries should be routed via CIPS. Every outbound payment must be supported by valid contracts, invoices, customs declarations where applicable, and a SAFE trade-verification record. The bank will screen against sanctions lists, denied-party lists, and trade-based money-laundering indicators.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with a PRC-licensed bank, limited to hedging actual contractual cash flow exposures and not exceeding the underlying transaction horizon
FX swaps between CNY and foreign currency for current-account cash-flow matching and liquidity rebalancing
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term USD/RMB liability or funding exposures, subject to SAFE derivative registration and real-exposure documentation
Vanilla FX options for hedging genuine current-account and approved capital-account exposures, with no speculative net positions

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore for the PRC WFOE; if the offshore parent enters into an NDF, it must remain strictly outside the WFOE's books and balance sheet to avoid derivative-access and regulatory violations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report (Market Entity Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Supervision Administration via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 of each calendar year for the immediately preceding fiscal year; no anniversary extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operation; if correction is not made within 3 years, inclusion in the List of Enterprises Subject to Serious Illegal Activity; continued non-operation for 6 consecutive months can trigger SAMR revocation of the business license (administrative strike-off), plus personal credit restrictions against the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) integrated with State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the joint NECIPS reporting window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 of each calendar year, filed simultaneously with the Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, or submission of false/incomplete foreign investment information, triggers a correction order with a 15-day cure period; continued refusal attracts an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000; repeated serious violations can result in cancellation of registration and loss of foreign-investment standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Final Settlement (CIT final reconciliation) with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) / local competent tax service bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the December 31 fiscal year end, i.e., on or before May 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to RMB 2,000 (up to RMB 10,000 in serious cases); late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day (approximately 18.25% per annum) on the unpaid CIT; under-reporting or tax evasion penalties of 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid; enforced collection measures include freezing of bank accounts, attachment of assets, exit taxation gates, and blocking of deregistration and outward remittance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements and Certified CPA Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Prepared for shareholders and the board under the PRC Company Law; the audited report is required to support the SAMR annual return, the CIT final settlement, the foreign investment annual report, and any SAFE or bank cross-border remittance review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ends December 31; audited financial statements must be finalized no later than May 31 of the following year and, for shareholder approval, no later than 4 months after the fiscal year end (April 30).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Production of defective or unaudited annual financial statements renders the NECIPS annual report and CIT filing defective; false or fraudulent accounting statements trigger administrative penalties, CPA-report rejection, personal liability of directors and controlling persons, and potentially criminal liability for accounting fraud.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation and 30-Day Change Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the Anti-Money Laundering Administration under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), via the Market Entity Registration and Beneficial Owner Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation embedded in the January 1 through June 30 annual report window; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 calendar days of the triggering share transfer or control change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, false, or omitted UBO reporting is an anti-money-laundering regulatory violation; sanctions include correction orders, administrative fines, public inclusion in AML compliance alerts, banking relationship termination, blocked access to payment rails (Stripe, wire transfers), and personal enforcement against the statutory representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual Income Tax (IIT) Final Settlement Reporting for Resident and Expatriate Employees of the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) / local competent tax service bureau as withholding agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 1 through June 30 of each year for the prior tax year, using the employer withholding records and annual summary reconciliations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to RMB 2,000 (up to RMB 10,000 in serious cases); late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on any under-withheld IIT; failure to correctly withhold may expose the WFOE to administrative fines, enhanced tax inspection, and restrictions on payroll and social insurance processing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social Insurance Annual Contribution Base Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (HRSS) / Social Insurance Administration under the applicable municipality or province
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally required after publication of the local social-average-wage data in the second calendar quarter; in most major mainland municipalities, the annual declaration window falls between April and July of the contribution year and must follow the specific local HRSS circular.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare the correct annual contribution base can result in arrears assessments, late fees of 0.05% per day, administrative fines of up to 200% to 500% of unpaid premiums, restriction of visa and work permits, and inclusion on the enterprise social insurance noncompliance list.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law and the Regulations on Enterprise Financial Accounting Reports, there is no general size-based SME audit exemption for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE). The mandatory CPA audit trigger is the WFOE legal entity itself: total assets greater than zero, annual turnover greater than zero, or headcount of one or more is sufficient to require an independent Chinese certified public accountant audit. In addition, a certified audit is expressly required whenever the tax authority, SAMR, MOFCOM, SAFE, a bank, an investor, or a lender requires audited financial statements; any WFOE with foreign exchange registration, cross-border share transfers, transfer-pricing risk, or consolidated international reporting is subject to the same mandatory annual audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance, substantially converged with IFRS; small-scale enterprises may apply the simplified PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, but the statutory audit opinion must still be issued under Chinese Standards on Auditing (CSAs). IFRS-alone reporting is not a substitute for PRC statutory reporting unless expressly accepted by the competent Chinese authority or required by a foreign parent for non-statutory consolidation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures effective November 1, 2024, the WFOE must identify and report every beneficial owner, being any natural or legal person holding or ultimately controlling 25% or more of the equity, voting rights, or control of the company. Beneficial owner information must be filed with SAMR and the anti-money-laundering administration at formation, updated within 30 calendar days of any qualifying change in ownership or control, and annually confirmed through the January 1 to June 30 NECIPS/USO annual report window. Even if there is no change, the annual nil confirmation is still compulsory. A stale UBO record will block annual AML/KYC banking renewal and can suspend payment rails including Stripe and wire transfers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300 to US$1,500 per year for a registered office/address or corporate agent service in most PRC provinces; US$1,500 to US$3,000 per year in Shanghai, Beijing, or Shenzhen for commercial address or agency packages.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,200 to US$4,000 for a low-risk SaaS WFOE with annual revenue below RMB 10 million and fewer than 20 employees; US$4,000 to US$12,000 per year if group consolidation, transfer-pricing documentation, or SAFE/foreign-exchange reporting is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Enterprise Income Tax rate for resident enterprises (EIT Law Article 4)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate for certified National High-Tech Enterprises; 20% effective rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with annual taxable income below RMB 3 million (reduced further to 2.5%-5% on the first RMB 1 million under current temporary policy; 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses under EIT Law Article 30 and SAT Announcement No. 28/2021; 10% preferential rate for key National Park / key software integrated circuit enterprises; 15% for Hainan Free Trade Port enterprises registered as encouraged industries; no specific patent box regime but R&D expense super-deduction provides equivalent innovation tax subsidy; loss carryforward of 5 years is supplemented by 10-year carryforward for qualifying high-tech and small-medium technology enterprises; preferential free-zone incentives available in Shanghai Lingang, Shenzhen Qianhai, and other State-level economic development zones for encouraged service industries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (A-type) '中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类）' - Form A100000 and supporting schedules A100000-A108020 filed electronically through the Electronic Taxation Bureau (e-Tax portal) at etax.chinatax.gov.cn; quarterly provisional prepayment returns are filed on Form A200000 within 15 days after the end of each quarter.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual reconciliation with quarterly (or monthly) provisional prepayments made during the taxable year; final annual return must be filed within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly pre-payment return due within 15 days after each quarter-end (April 15, July 15, October 15 and January 15); annual return and final declaration due by May 15 for a December 31 fiscal year-end (Article 54 EIT Law).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover derived from the logistics-telematics SaaS platform, fleet data subscription fees, dispatch optimization licensing, telematics hardware resale, and maintenance services, as recorded under Chinese Accounting Standards (CAS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue sourced in China for the Chinese WFOE; all contracts with non-resident clients must be mapped to the invoicing VAT and EIT reconciliation, ensure that receipt of foreign-currency payments is booked at Chinese central parity exchange rate; intercompany service revenues from overseas group companies must be tagged and substantiated with transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs including cloud server hosting, data connectivity, telematics device cost of goods sold, and direct labor of deployment engineers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reimbursements or cost reallocations from overseas headquarters are not allowed unless supported by a valid cost-sharing agreement and arm's-length allocation evidence; any related-party purchase of software or data fabrication services must be at arm's length and within BEPS action item 8-10 documentation files.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Business Taxes and Surcharges (税金及附加)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, property tax, stamp duty, and other consumption surcharges accrued alongside VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT withholding on imported software royalties and overseas SaaS payments (6% VAT withholding for intangible services) must be reconciled; customs-related duties on telematics hardware imports are not deductible as surcharges under this box and should be capitalized in inventory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, promotional fees, sales commissions, and business development expenses of the fleet dispatch platform.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border marketing service fees paid to foreign resellers are deductible only if proven at arm's length and subject to a 10% withholding tax on service fees if attributable to foreign enterprise for China-source services; commission invoices from overseas agents must include a valid contract and beneficial ownership declaration for DTA exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management, legal, accounting, R&D, licensing, and general office expenses; includes salaries of directors and employees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign headquarters general and administrative allocations (headcount, IT support, corporate branding) are deductible only if the foreign service provider has comprehensive supporting evidence, dual-affiliation arrangement, and no mere cost-pass-through; labor costs for expatriate directors working in China must be recorded and subject to individual income tax; R&D expenses attributable to the Chinese WFOE's software code development qualify for the 100% super-deduction in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on bank loans, intercompany borrowings, late-payment interest, and bank transaction fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to overseas affiliates is considered China-source income and subject to 10% statutory withholding (or lower DTA treaty rate); the debt-to-equity thin capitalization ratio of 2:1 must be respected under EIT Law Article 46; failing to demonstrate the use of funds for the Chinese WFOE's business will disallow the interest deduction and invoke withholding penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Total Profit and Taxable Income (利润总额与应纳税所得额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summation of operating profit, non-operating income and non-operating expenses. AADD schedule adjustments such as entertainment expenses, related-party interest consumption, R&D super-deduction, business entertainment cost limits, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be aware that dividends distributed after this taxable income is calculated are subject to a 10% withholding tax; all legal adjustments for DTA-protected income (e.g., treaty-exempt interest) must be declared in Schedule A105000; a failure to file Schedule A107012 for R&D super-deduction will increase effective tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary schedule for non-resident income categories: dividends, interest, royalties, leases, service fees, and capital gains paid to foreign shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE, as withholding agent, must file the withholding declaration within 7 days after the income is paid; treaty relief requires completed Form 501, valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction J, and a beneficial ownership statement; failure to withhold subjects the WFOE to a 50%-3x penalty on the withheld amount plus daily 0.05% interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission of quarterly or annual enterprise income tax returns triggers a RMB 2,000 non-compliance fine (up to RMB 10,000 for severe cases) under Article 62 of the Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL). An underpayment of provisional tax creates a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid amount under TCAL Article 32. For fraudulent under-declaration of taxable income, TCAL Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax plus criminal reference; deliberate omission causing tax loss in excess of RMB 100,000 and 10% of taxable income triggers the criminal threshold under Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to 3 years or detention, escalating to 3-7 years for large-amount evasion. Failure to file related-party transaction documentation (Form A100000) or misleading schedules brings penalty of RMB 10,000 and simultaneous adjustments with interest.
